Sam (acme-app): Hey team — over the last 30m ~20% of our requests are getting ~800ms extra latency and occasional 502s. We traced it: our telemetry shows most hits going to us-east-1 instead of eu-west-1.
Alyssa (support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a curl or example request you send? do you set any region header/param? :thinking_face:
Sam (acme-app): We set a custom header X-Preferred-Region: ["eu-west-1"] (our SDK serializes it as a JSON array). Also we set ?region=eu-west-1 in some older calls for compatibility. Most traffic is the header form.
Alyssa (support): hm ok. leaving this to eng-oncall to check routing priority. tagging @Jamie
Jamie (eng-oncall): grabbing logs for the client IP you sent. quick question: do you also send a cookie like region=us-east or any proxy that might add headers?
Sam (acme-app): There is a legacy cookie region=us-east set by an old proxy. We forgot to clear it when switching envs.
Ricardo (infra): that could explain a fallback cascade. Router priority currently: 1) explicit query param ?region, 2) header X-Region or X-Client-Region (single token), 3) cookie, 4) geo-IP. Your header (X-Preferred-Region) is not in the recognized header list so router ignored it and then saw cookie=us-east and routed to us-east.
Jamie (eng-oncall): Confirmed in the debug trace for request id abc123: headers show X-Preferred-Region: ["eu-west-1"], Cookie: region=us-east; router_log: selected_region=us-east (cookie precedence).
Alyssa (support): that matches customer repro. Sam — quick mitigation: remove the legacy cookie or set ?region=eu-west-1 in your request.
Sam (acme-app): we can clear cookie but worried about long rollout across clients. any server-side fixes? our backend really wants to honor X-Preferred-Region.
Ricardo (infra): short-term: we can add X-Preferred-Region as an alias to recognized headers and normalize JSON arrays by taking the first non-empty element. patch I have in mind: in routing header normalization step, add acceptedAliases += ["x-preferred-region"], and if header value matches /^\[.*\]$/, parse and extract first entry trim quotes.
Jamie (eng-oncall): I can push a config change to the canary edge to accept the alias and array normalization. Will need a quick deploy approval. deploy-bot: queued deploy for edge-canary (config-only) by jamie — runbook check passed.
deploy-bot: deployed edge-canary config v2026.03.17-rc1 — routing aliases updated.
Jamie (eng-oncall): Sam, can you retry a few requests (curl below) and let us know if they land in eu-west and latency drops?
Sam (acme-app): trying now...
Sam (acme-app): curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H "X-Preferred-Region: ["eu-west-1"]" 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?prompt=hello&region= ' (we intentionally left ?region blank in some calls)
Jamie (eng-oncall): I see requests from your IP hitting eu-west in the canary logs and 200s with ~60ms token latency. router_log: selected_region=eu-west-1, reason=header_alias_matched (x-preferred-region).
Sam (acme-app): looks good in our dashboard, latency back to expected. :tada: any billing impact from prior misroutes? we saw cross-region egress spikes to us-east yesterday.
Alyssa (support): I'll open billing escalation to check egress charges during the window when cookie forced us-east.
Ricardo (infra): note: we only normalize arrays on accepted aliases for now. If you send both the cookie and header, cookie still wins per precedence rules. If you want header to always override cookie, we can discuss changing precedence but that's a policy decision.
Sam (acme-app): understood — we'll remove legacy cookie from clients within 72h. temporary patch works. thank you all.
Jamie (eng-oncall): action items: 1) roll canary alias change to prod after 1hr of canary telemetry (me), 2) support create billing ticket (Alyssa), 3) infra doc update about accepted header aliases and JSON-array normalization (Ricardo).
Alyssa (support): added billing ticket #B-8931 and flagged for review. Sam — if you want a credit review, add a short summary of load and time window.
Sam (acme-app): will do. Thanks everyone! :pray:
